svg.aria-label: Preflight timeline: the procurement-to-silicon window with and without preflight
svg.title: Preflight timeline: the procurement-to-silicon window with and without preflight
svg.text: The ~3 month procurement-to-silicon window
WITHOUT preflight
Months 1-3: hardware in procurement.
Engineers idle on integration.
Silicon lands.
Integration failures found HERE: operator install,
resource advertisement, DRA, telemetry, versions.
Then the hardware-dependent validation begins.
WITH preflight [dashed border]
Months 1-3: AICR runs UNMODIFIED on a Mokka fleet.
16 of 21 checks are analytically capable of real signal.
Integration failures found and fixed HERE.
Measured in this sweep: 3 real passes, and 1 genuine
catch of a version-constraint violation.
Silicon lands. Hardware time goes to the 4 checks that
REQUIRE it: 3x NCCL plus inference-perf.
What this diagram deliberately does NOT show
No "day-one first token". Simulation does not prove it: the path that determines first token
(CUDA execution, NCCL data plane, TTFT) is exactly the path preflight cannot exercise.
Measured 2026-08-03. AICR dispatched 9 of 21 checks on this cluster; 3 passed. The distance to the 16-check
ceiling is host memory (7.75 GiB held 2 of 14 recipe components), not a Mokka limitation.
No bring-up-time saving is drawn or claimed: that needs a real bring-up failure history to back-test against,
and that data was not available. AICR-on-silicon remains the final readiness gate.
